# Let me understand the full ring structure and figure out the goal
# First, let me see what the green arrows do by probing one

seg = current_frame.segmentation

for n in seg['nodes']:
    if n['pixels'] == 4:
        br = n['boundary'][0]
        current_blocks[(br[0], br[1])] = n['color']

# Click top-right green arrow at (16, 38)

    if n['pixels'] == 4:
        br = n['boundary'][0]
        new_blocks[(br[0], br[1])] = n['color']

changed = []
for pos in current_blocks:
    if pos in new_blocks:
        if current_blocks[pos] != new_blocks[pos]:
            changed.append((pos, current_blocks[pos], new_blocks[pos]))

print(f"Changed blocks ({len(changed)}):")
for c in changed:
    print(f"  {c}")

# Check Y positions
y_blocks = []
for n in seg2['nodes']:
    if n['color'] == 'Y' and n['pixels'] == 4:
        br = n['boundary'][0]
